correctness.rationale: Exact Dirichlet integration yields the moments and positive-factor covariance formula, verified by 72 rational exhaustive occupancy calculations. A gamma-ratio decomposition gives uniform h bounds, forcing sign separation globally and strict decrease through the only possible transition window for every sufficiently large m with fixed 0<gamma<1. The differentiable interpolation and second-order expansion give the O(1) location and O(m^-1/2) error; nine high-precision roots corroborate. The c sqrt(m) limit is uniform on compact positive c windows, not over varying gamma.

originality.rationale: The strongest classical prior exact joint sampling formula (Huillet 2005; Huillet–Paroissin 2008) is acknowledged and used, not rebranded as new. The inspected primary text and index records do not state the global large-m covariance one-crossing theorem or precise square-root cutoff and offset. The result is a nontrivial uniform qualitative deduction rather than a special parameter substitution; uninspected primary sections could still implicitly cover it.
residual_risks: The full 2005 finite-Dirichlet sampling paper was not read, so an implicit asymptotic sign statement cannot be excluded.

Exact joint sampling probabilities in the classical literature logically entail the factorial moments; novelty is restricted to a global growing-sample phase classification and constant-order boundary term.
Database and targeted web search are not exhaustive mathematical uniqueness certificates.

value.rationale: The sign of covariance between singleton and doubleton frequency counts is relevant to interpretation of rare-category spectra in finite populations. Fixed-size infinite-Ewens conclusions fail precisely at order sqrt(number of available species). A global eventual one-crossing theorem and the sharp additive shift distinguish it from a routine covariance calculation or arbitrary parameter slice.
